segments: 3 Chronography of Barhebraeus.
Andronicus, the tyrant of Constantinople,
when [he decided] to kill Isaac also (Isaac, a certain man from the nobles, who alone was left from the stock of King Manuel),
Isaac fortified himself in his house.
And when Andronicus sent the commander of the army to summon Isaac to him,
Isaac defied him, drew a sword, and killed the commander of the army.
And he mounted his horse and went out to go to the Great Church, with his sword in his hand dripping with blood,
and he was crying out and lamenting.
And tens of thousands of the people joined him, and also many nobles who had stumbled at the tyrant.
And they entered the church,
and they compelled the Patriarch,
and he consecrated Isaac as king.
Now when the tyrant heard [this],
he went out from the palace to flee by sea.
And they overtook him and brought him back to Constantinople.
And they cut up his flesh while he was still alive with small knives {OCR?} and gnawed [it].
And after great torments, they burned him with fire in the midst of the assembly.
And in that same year, when the disease of elephantiasis grew severe upon Baldwin, king of Jerusalem,
he surrendered the kingdom to a child (to the child {OCR?}), his sister's son,
who was also called Baldwin (the Fifth {OCR?});
and he died.
And in the year 582 [of the Greeks / AH],
582 of the Arabs [1186 AD]:
Saladin recovered his health and went from Harran to Aleppo,
and from there to Homs.
And he found that Nasir al-Din, the son of his brother Shams al-Dawlah, was dead.
And he took the fortress of Homs from his son,
and found in it great wealth.
And from there he went to Damascus.
And he turned and took Aleppo from his brother al-Adil,
and gave it to al-Malik al-Zahir, his son.
And he gave Damascus to al-Malik al-Afdal, his other son.
And he gave Egypt to al-Malik al-Aziz, his other son,
and sent him to Egypt,
and with him his brother al-Adil.
Now Taqi al-Din, his brother's son, who was there,
when he heard that Egypt had gone out of his hand,
took offense and prepared to go to Africa.
However, Saladin sent to trouble him [dissuade him] and brought him to himself,
and pacified his heart (his mind {OCR?}),
as though because of his valor he desired him to be with him.
And he gave him Hama, Ma'arrat, Salamiyah, Manbij, and Qal'at Najm;
and he added to him Mayperqat also.
